ecosystemSandboxPage.title: Ecosystem Sandbox Simulation
ecosystemSandboxPage.subtitle: High-performance pure frontend ecosystem simulation demo
ecosystemSandboxPage.clickToAdd: Click on the sandbox area to add organisms
ecosystemSandboxPage.rulesSubtitle: Understand ecosystem mechanisms, observe organism survival, evolution and interaction
ecosystemSandboxPage.hungerMechanismDesc: Each organism has a hunger value of 0-100 that decreases over time. When hungry, organisms accelerate food search; when extremely hungry, they slow down or die.
ecosystemSandboxPage.basicOrganismDesc: Initial organism type, blue-green color scheme (from blue-green to cyan). Moderate hunger consumption, medium speed, can evolve into other advanced types.
ecosystemSandboxPage.predatorDesc: Red color scheme (red to orange-red), with inner circle marker. Faster speed, larger perception range, but faster hunger consumption, top consumer in the ecosystem.
ecosystemSandboxPage.scavengerDesc: Purple color scheme (purple to pink-purple), with semicircle marker. More efficient food consumption, slower hunger consumption, efficient survivor in the ecosystem.
ecosystemSandboxPage.evolutionDesc: When basic organisms reach 500 frames of age and hunger value above 60, they have a chance to evolve into predators or scavengers. After evolution, they gain new traits and appearance markers.
ecosystemSandboxPage.deathCycleDesc: When hunger value drops to 0, organisms die and have a 70% chance to transform into new food, forming an ecological cycle and maintaining system balance.
ecosystemSandboxPage.reproductionDesc: When organisms reach 200 frames of age and hunger value above 70, they enter reproduction state and seek mates. Reproducing organisms move closer and remain relatively still, after completion new organisms are born at random positions around parents. Reproduction probability is affected by terrain.
ecosystemSandboxPage.inheritanceDesc: Newly born organisms inherit parent type and some traits, but also have slight random variations, forming biodiversity.
ecosystemSandboxPage.oceanDesc: Organisms can pass through ocean areas, move faster in ocean (3x base speed). Cannot spawn organisms or food in ocean. Faster hunger consumption (200%), very low reproduction probability (10%), no health recovery. Organisms have slight blue tint.
ecosystemSandboxPage.beachDesc: Lower food generation rate (0.7x base), normal organism movement speed, suitable for basic organism survival, relatively low evolution probability. Slightly faster hunger consumption (120%), slightly higher reproduction probability (120%), slight health recovery. Organisms have beach tint.
ecosystemSandboxPage.forestDesc: High food generation rate (1.3x base), faster organism movement speed (1.1x base), high organism density, increased evolution probability, most active area in ecosystem. Slower hunger consumption (90%), high reproduction probability (150%), moderate health recovery. Organisms have green tint.
ecosystemSandboxPage.mountainDesc: Organisms cannot jump over or pass through mountains, they will be blocked. If organisms spawn on mountains, movement speed is greatly reduced (30% of base). Cannot spawn food on mountains. Faster hunger consumption (150%), but high health recovery rate (1.5%/frame). Organisms have gray tint.
ecosystemSandboxPage.plainsDesc: Moderate food generation rate (1.1x base), fastest organism movement speed (1.3x base), predators can maximize advantage in this area, suitable for fast movement and hunting. Normal hunger consumption, higher reproduction probability (130%), slight health recovery. Organisms have grassland green tint.
ecosystemSandboxPage.terrainAdaptationDesc: Different terrains affect organism movement ability, speed, hunger consumption, reproduction probability, health recovery and food detection ability. Mountain areas have passage restrictions, organisms cannot pass through these obstacles. Ocean areas organisms can pass through, but have other special effects. Each terrain has unique ecological characteristics that affect organism survival strategies.
ecosystemSandboxPage.zoomFeatureDesc: Hover mouse over sandbox area, hold Ctrl key and scroll mouse wheel to zoom in or out. Zoom limit is 1x-3x, centered on mouse position.
ecosystemSandboxPage.dragPanDesc: After zooming in, you can click and drag mouse to pan sandbox view, mouse cursor will change to grab state indicating draggable.
ecosystemSandboxPage.resetViewDescDesc: Use the "Reset View" button in control panel to restore map to original scale and position with one click.
ecosystemSandboxPage.operationGuideDesc: Click on sandbox area to add organisms, use control panel to adjust speed, add/reset organisms and food, and control ecosystem state.
